title: Canva’s first AI image model plans designs before generating them
content:
Canva is diving even deeper into AI with the launch of an image generation model that competes directly with those from OpenAI, Microsoft, and Google. The model, called Canva Craft, uses a two-stage architecture that allows it to plan a design before generating an image, allowing for “greater precision, consistency and control,” according to an announcement on Thursday.
Canva’s first AI image model plans designs before generating them
Canva Craft can generate images at up to 2K resolution and in more than 30 aspect ratios.
Canva Craft can generate images at up to 2K resolution and in more than 30 aspect ratios. In addition to generating social media posts and marketing content, it’s also supposed to create realistic scenes, digital art, environmental imagery, and more. The model’s two-stage system allows it to more accurately generate complex images that require legible text and precise object placement, according to Canva.
The new AI model builds on Canva’s big push into AI. In April, Canva launched new prompt-based editing capabilities that allow you to create or make changes to a design by describing it. The design tool also brought layers to AI-generated images, which let you make changes to part of an image while leaving the rest untouched.
Canva says it trained Craft on “millions of human-made templates” from the platform’s content library, which includes things like social media posts, presentations, infographics, and menus. The model is currently ranked fourth on Design Arena’s leaderboard for the best AI image generation models, a crowdsourced benchmark for AI designs. It sits behind OpenAI’s GPT-Image-2.5 Sunburst, GPT-Image-2.5 Flare, and GPT-Image-2.
Canva notes that its AI model comes with “robust input and output moderation, privacy and safety controls, and reporting tools.” The company plans to allow AI agents to plug into Canva Craft through the open Model Context Protocol, and will also roll out more efficient Craft-fast and Craft-ultrafast models in the future.
Canva Craft is available now to all users globally. You can try it by navigating to the three-dot option on Canva’s left-hand menu and then selecting Dream Lab.

report.summary: Canva launched Craft, its first in-house AI image model that plans designs before generating, offering up to 2K resolution and 30+ aspect ratios.
report.background: Canva has been expanding from a template-based design platform into an AI-powered creative suite. In April, it introduced prompt-based editing and layered AI-generated images, letting users modify parts of a design without regenerating everything. Craft marks a bigger step: Canva is building its own image model rather than relying solely on partners, putting it in direct competition with OpenAI, Microsoft, and Google. Canva says it trained Craft on millions of human-made templates from its library, including social posts, presentations, infographics, and menus. The two-stage architecture is intended to improve control over layout, text, and object placement. Craft is already ranked fourth on Design Arena’s crowdsourced leaderboard, behind three OpenAI GPT-Image models, suggesting Canva can compete technically while leveraging its design-workflow distribution.
key_points: Craft uses a two-stage architecture: it first plans a design, then generates the image. Canva says this gives greater precision, consistency, and control, especially for complex images that require legible text and precise object placement. The approach differs from typical one-shot image generators that jump straight from prompt to pixels.

The model generates images at up to 2K resolution and supports more than 30 aspect ratios. Canva positions it for social media posts, marketing content, realistic scenes, digital art, environmental imagery, and other design tasks. That breadth fits Canva’s core audience of marketers, creators, and small businesses.

Canva trained Craft on millions of human-made templates from its content library, including presentations, menus, and infographics. On Design Arena’s crowdsourced benchmark, Craft ranks fourth, behind OpenAI’s GPT-Image-2.5 Sunburst, GPT-Image-2.5 Flare, and GPT-Image-2. The ranking suggests strong quality but not category leadership yet.

Canva says Craft includes robust input and output moderation, privacy and safety controls, and reporting tools. The company plans to let AI agents connect through the open Model Context Protocol and will release faster Craft-fast and Craft-ultrafast variants later. Craft is available globally now through Dream Lab in Canva’s three-dot menu.
report.impact: Canva Craft signals that design platforms are moving from AI features to in-house foundation models. For the AI industry, it adds a vertical competitor that pairs model development with a huge existing design workflow and template library. For developers, Canva’s planned Model Context Protocol support could make Craft accessible to AI agents and external tools, creating new integration opportunities. For regular users, the planning-first approach may deliver more reliable text rendering and object placement, reducing the frustrating iteration common with image generators. The bigger shift is distribution: Canva can embed Craft directly where millions already create marketing and social content, pressuring standalone image-model providers to differentiate on quality, APIs, and agent ecosystems rather than access alone.
report.tools: Try Canva Craft through Canva’s Dream Lab via the three-dot menu. Follow Design Arena’s leaderboard to compare image models. For open-source experimentation, ComfyUI with Stable Diffusion or Flux workflows can approximate staged generation and layout control; Ideogram is worth watching for text-heavy images. Developers interested in agent integrations should track Canva’s Model Context Protocol rollout and MCP-compatible clients.
